title: B2 · L50 — B2 review & mixed
description: Práctica mixta B2: condicionales, inversión, phrasal verbs, idiomas, hedging, register. Consolidación de los 49 packs anteriores antes de pasar a B2+.

questions.prompt: Explicas a un colega por qué llegaste tarde tras quedar atrapado en un atasco brutal.
questions.question: Complete (third conditional): 'If I ___ the traffic report, I ___ this route.'
questions.explanation: Tercer condicional puro: 'if + past perfect (had heard)' + 'would (not) have + PP (wouldn't have taken)'. Situación pasada IRREAL con consecuencia CONTRARIA a lo que ocurrió (sí escogí esta ruta, no oí el parte). Error clásico: mezclar tiempos de otros condicionales. Regla oro: 'would have' NUNCA va después de 'if' en registro estándar.
examples: If I had checked the map, I wouldn't have got lost on the way. → arrepentimiento
If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam. → consecuencia hipotética

questions.prompt: Escribes en un discurso conmovedor sobre una experiencia única.
questions.question: Which uses correct formal inversion with 'Never'?
options: Never I had felt so proud in my life.
Never had I felt so proud in my life.
I never had felt so proud in my life.
Had I never felt so proud in my life.
questions.explanation: Con adverbios negativos al inicio ('Never', 'Rarely', 'Seldom', 'Not until'), se INVIERTE auxiliar + sujeto: 'Never HAD I felt' (no 'I had felt'). Estructura formal-enfática, muy usada en discursos, literatura, escritura ceremonial. Distractores: A y C no invierten (agramatical con 'never' inicial); D confunde con inversión condicional. Sin la inversión, el énfasis desaparece.
examples: Never had I imagined such a beautiful sight. → énfasis literario
Rarely does she complain, even under pressure. → inversión con adverbio de frecuencia

questions.prompt: Escribes: 'Despite the rain, we went out.'
questions.statement: 'Despite the rain, we went out' es gramaticalmente correcto.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Estructura: 'Despite + noun/-ing' (never 'Despite + subject + verb'). CORRECTO: 'Despite the rain' o 'Despite raining'. INCORRECTO: *'Despite it rained' — error clásico de hispanohablante por calco de 'a pesar de que llovió'. Regla oro: 'despite' e 'in spite of' son PREPOSICIONES, seguidas de sustantivo/-ing. Para clausula completa, usa 'although' o 'even though' + subject + verb.
examples: Despite the noise, I slept well. → despite + noun
In spite of being tired, he kept working. → in spite of + -ing

questions.text: Having lived abroad for many years, she has developed a truly international perspective.
questions.explanation: Cláusula de participio perfecto — estructura ELEGANTE de escritura formal. Connected speech: 'Having lived' fluye 'HAV-ing-LIVD'; 'truly international' — stress marcado en 'TRUE-ly'. Estructura: 'Having + PP' + subject + main clause. Función: introducir experiencia previa que explica situación actual. Alternativa: 'Because she has lived abroad, she has developed...' — más largo, menos elegante. Registro académico-profesional.
examples: Having graduated with honours, she started her career at McKinsey. → experiencia previa
Having worked overseas for a decade, he speaks four languages fluently. → causa-efecto elegante

questions.prompt: Enviaste un email en caliente y ahora te arrepientes profundamente.
questions.question: 'I wish I ___ that email yesterday.' (regret about the past)
questions.explanation: 'Wish + past perfect (hadn't sent)' expresa arrepentimiento POR ACCIÓN PASADA ya consumada. Equivale al español 'ojalá no lo hubiera enviado'. Error típico: usar past simple ('I wish I didn't send'), que suena a rutina pasada, no a arrepentimiento puntual. Regla oro: past perfect después de 'wish' = arrepentimiento; past simple = deseo presente irreal.
examples: I wish I had studied harder for that exam. → arrepentimiento académico
I wish I hadn't said that in the meeting. → arrepentimiento social

questions.prompt: Un artículo periodístico dice: 'The building was said to have been designed by a famous architect.'
questions.statement: 'The building was said to have been designed by a famous architect' usa correctamente la pasiva avanzada.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Estructura de DOBLE PASIVA reportativa: 'was said' + 'to have been + PP'. Función: reportar información pasada de forma impersonal y elegante. Muy común en periodismo, informes históricos, textos académicos. Alternativa activa: 'People said the building had been designed by...' (menos elegante). Verbos que aceptan esta estructura: say, think, believe, report, know, allege, rumour.
examples: He is thought to have left the country before the trial. → deducción impersonal
The document is believed to have been destroyed intentionally. → reporte cauto

questions.prompt: Empareja cada inicio con su continuación (idioms + fórmulas B2):
questions.explanation: Repaso mixto de idiomas y fórmulas B2 aprendidas a lo largo del nivel: PARTES DEL CUERPO ('arm and leg', 'pain in the neck'), ANIMALES ('cat out of the bag'), COLORES ('out of the blue'), ACUERDO ENFÁTICO ('couldn't agree more'). Cada uno tiene función precisa. Reconocerlos y usarlos con naturalidad es señal de que has interiorizado el nivel B2.
examples: That car cost an arm and a leg — worth every penny though. → gasto extremo
The news came out of the blue — nobody saw it coming. → sorpresa total

questions.prompt: En un informe formal, analizas la probabilidad de un cambio de decisión.
questions.question: Complete: 'It is ___ that this decision will be reversed.'
questions.explanation: Estructura correcta: 'It is UNLIKELY THAT + clause' (sujeto + verbo). ALTERNATIVA con estructura diferente: 'It is unlikely TO + infinitive' pero cambia el sujeto ('It' se refiere a la acción abstracta). Distractores: 'unlikely to' necesita infinitivo directo, no 'that'; 'unlike' es preposición ('unlike me...'); 'not likely to' es agramatical con 'It is'. Regla: elige la estructura completa según lo que sigue.
examples: It is unlikely that prices will drop before Christmas. → probabilidad + clause
Prices are unlikely to drop before Christmas. → alternativa con sujeto real

questions.target: Had I known you were looking for a job, I would have put you in touch with my contact at that company.
questions.explanation: Combinación magistral: INVERSIÓN CONDICIONAL ('Had I known' = 'If I had known') + TERCER CONDICIONAL ('would have put'). Registro formal-profesional. Vocabulario clave: 'put someone in touch with' = poner en contacto = conectar profesionalmente. En hablado, ritmo mesurado, tono de disculpa cortés. Contracciones opcionales — ligeramente formal. Frase muy útil en networking cuando descubres que podrías haber ayudado.
examples: Had I realised how tight the deadline was, I would have started earlier. → arrepentimiento con inversión
Had she asked me directly, I would have said yes without hesitation. → hipótesis retrospectiva

questions.prompt: Presentas una idea al equipo pero quieres sugerirla sin imponerla.
questions.question: Which is a HEDGED (uncertain, softened) statement?
options: It will definitely happen no matter what.
It may be worth considering as an option.
There's no doubt about it at all.
questions.explanation: 'May be worth considering' es DOBLE HEDGING: 'may' (posibilidad, no certeza) + 'worth considering' (sugerencia, no imposición). Suaviza al máximo sin renunciar a la propuesta. Perfecto para meetings donde no quieres parecer autoritario. Los distractores son afirmaciones ABSOLUTAS que suenan dogmáticas — opuestas al hedging. Alternativas equivalentes: 'It might be worth trying', 'Perhaps we could consider...', 'It could be an idea to...'.
examples: It might be worth trying a different approach next quarter. → sugerencia hedged
Perhaps we could consider outsourcing this task. → propuesta suavizada

questions.prompt: Alguien dice: 'What she really needs is more support.'
questions.statement: 'What she really needs is more support' es una cleft sentence.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Estructura de WH-CLEFT: 'What + subject + verb + IS/WAS + resto'. Función: ENFATIZAR el elemento que sigue a 'is'. Muy usada en conversación y escritura para destacar necesidades, deseos o hechos. Alternativas equivalentes: 'She really needs MORE SUPPORT' (mismo significado, menos énfasis); 'It's more support that she really needs' (cleft con 'it', foco identificativo). Recurso característico del inglés B2/C1.
examples: What I need is a proper break — a real holiday. → cleft con necesidad
What he wants is recognition, not just money. → cleft con contraste

questions.text: I'm afraid we're going to have to postpone the meeting until further notice.
questions.explanation: Comunicación profesional mala noticia. Connected speech: 'I'm afraid' fluye 'aɪm-ə-FREID'; 'we're going to have to' colapsa 'wɪr-gonna-hafta'. Fórmulas clave: 'I'm afraid' (disculpa anticipada), 'have to postpone' (obligación educada), 'until further notice' (sin fecha concreta). Combinación muy profesional. Vocabulario técnico: 'until further notice' = hasta nuevo aviso — fórmula fija muy útil en comunicación corporativa.
examples: I'm afraid we can't accommodate that request at this time. → rechazo cortés
The event has been postponed until further notice due to weather. → aviso oficial

questions.prompt: Un americano te dice apurado: 'Sorry, I'm gonna have to run — huge meeting.'
questions.question: 'I'm gonna have to run' — this uses:
questions.explanation: 'Gonna' es REDUCCIÓN natural de 'going to' — típica del habla informal americana e internacional. NO se escribe en registro formal (email profesional, contrato) pero se usa MUCHO en oral y mensajería casual. Otras reducciones familia: 'gotta' (got to), 'wanna' (want to), 'kinda' (kind of). Reconocerlas al oír es clave para comprensión del habla nativa. Distractores confunden con otros conceptos gramaticales.
examples: I'm gonna call her later today — after the meeting. → informal casual
I gotta go — see you tomorrow at the office. → phrasal reduction típico

questions.target: To sum up, while there are certainly challenges ahead, I firmly believe we have the resources and talent to overcome them.
questions.explanation: Cierre magistral de discurso profesional. Estructura: SEÑAL DE CIERRE ('to sum up') + CONCESIÓN ('while... challenges') + TESIS FIRME ('I firmly believe') + OPTIMISMO CONCRETO ('resources and talent to overcome'). Fórmula típica de discurso B2/C1 evaluada en Cambridge FCE Speaking. En hablado, ritmo pausado, tono confiado, énfasis en 'FIRMLY BELIEVE'. Contracciones opcionales — ligeramente formal.
examples: To sum up, the outlook is challenging but genuinely positive. → cierre balanceado
While there are risks, the potential upside is enormous for us. → concesión + optimismo

questions.prompt: Comparas diferentes formas de despedirte al salir de una reunión.
questions.question: Which sentence is most FORMAL?
options: Kindly note that I must take my leave.
questions.explanation: 'Kindly note that I must take my leave' es lenguaje formal-arcaico, casi ceremonial. Uso: correspondencia oficial, discursos, contextos muy formales o irónicos. Los distractores son coloquiales: A informal americano ('gotta'); C informal británico ('I'm off'); D informal-arcaico americano ('see ya'). En la práctica moderna, este nivel de formalidad se reserva para muy pocos contextos. Reconocer el registro correcto para cada situación es habilidad B2 clave.
examples: Kindly note the following changes to the schedule. → registro formal escrito
I must take my leave now — thank you for your time. → despedida ceremonial
